title: POC scoping - Cost modeling & benchmarks with Zenith Tech
summary: POC scoping to align on success criteria, workload sizing and an executable 4-week benchmark plan focused on per-token unit economics. Agreed baseline traffic shape, target SLAs, and next steps to share cost model and run an initial benchmark on Redwood hosted and Dedicated variants.
topics: Workload sizing: QPS, concurrent users, token distribution
Benchmarks: scripts, datasets, and metrics to capture
Unit economics: per-token estimates, 1k-token price equivalents
Batching/caching knobs: expected hit rates and effects
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-05
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Aisha (Zenith Head of ML), Samir (CTO), Lena (Infra), Tom (PM)

Summary (auto): POC scope agreed: 4-week bench, gather 1 week of production traces, run hosted and dedicated runs, target cost and latency thresholds.

00:00 - Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intro - im maya, ae on the account, diego is our se, we want to run through your workloads and nail down the cost model for the poc
00:18 - Aisha: thanks, we have about 10k daily active users, maybe 100 concurrent at peak, most calls are short form summarizations and a smaller percent are long-form generation
00:32 - Samir: important for us is the unit economics — we operate on tight margins so per token cost + caching savings matter a lot
00:46 - Diego: great, that's exactly what this call is for. can you walk us through the typical request size and distribution?
01:05 - Aisha: yeah typical prompt is 120 tokens, average generation 280 tokens so ~400 tokens per request on average. 75% of requests are under 300 tokens, 25% are > 500 tokens
01:23 - Tom: we also have a conversational flow where context grows, so if there's prefix caching that can cut cost that'd be huge
01:40 - Diego: noted, prefix/K-V cache can drop repeated context decode cost a lot. what's your p95 latency target for full response?
01:55 - Samir: p95 end-to-end ideally under 2s for the typical 400-token workload; token streaming faster is ok but p95 end-to-end is the SLA measure
02:12 - Maya: ok SLA target p95 < 2000ms, and budget wise what ballpark are you thinking?
02:22 - Samir: we have an initial monthly budget for the POC/early pilot of $5k to $15k depending on findings; long term we'd like sub-$0.10 per MAU incremental but for tokens we need a per-token model
02:38 - Diego: we'll produce a per-1k-token and per-token estimate for hosted vs dedicated and show delta with caching and batching. initial numbers we use for planning today: hosted baseline ~ $0.10 per 1k tokens, dedicated reserved could be ~ $0.03 per 1k tokens depending on commit and utilization — we'll run actual benchmark for more accurate numbers
03:05 - Lena: those hosted numbers seem high compared to our current self-hosted, but remember you handle infra and ops which we value; curious how batching factors in
03:20 - Diego: batching reduces GPU overhead - effective unit cost improves with batch sizes of 8-32 depending on model and latency constraints. we typically see 1.5-3x unit cost improvement from smart batching for throughput-oriented workloads. dynamic batching preserves latency SLO by not waiting long for full bins
03:45 - Aisha: and caching? how much can we realistically expect given our conversational patterns?
04:00 - Diego: depends on repeatability of prefixes. With conversation prefix caching (KV cache) hit rates of 20-40% are common for apps with repeated system prompts or templates; with templated prompts you can push 50%+ in some cases. each cache hit amortizes the cost of prompt encoding and some decode, often 2x-5x cost reduction on those requests
04:28 - Tom: can you show an example cost model?
04:35 - Maya: sure — example for planning: if avg request = 400 tokens, 100 qps sustained, that's 40k tokens/sec or ~2.4M tokens/min. At hosted $0.10 per 1k tokens that is $240/month? wait we'll do math here: 2.4M tokens/min -> 3,456M tokens/day? (Maya stumbles)
05:10 - (laughter)
05:12 - Diego: quick correction, let's normalize: 100 qps * 400 tokens = 40k tokens/sec -> 2.4M tokens/min -> 144M tokens/hr -> 3,456M tokens/day -> multiply by 30 -> ~103.6B tokens/month. At $0.10 per 1k tokens that's $10,360 per month — numbers scaled with traffic. for POC we scope lower traffic; we'll run exact trace-based simulation
06:00 - Samir: ok that helps — so per-1k price matters a lot. if dedicated gets to $0.03 per 1k that would be ~ $3,108 per month at same volume, not including reserved commit amortization
06:20 - Aisha: we also want to understand latency differences between hosted and dedicated and the overhead of quantized models
06:30 - Diego: onsite/dedicated typically gives better throughput and more predictable p95 because you control infra; quantization (4-bit/8-bit) can reduce GPU memory and increase effective throughput, sometimes with minor quality delta. we'll include model variants: fp16, 8-bit, and 4-bit int8/int4 runs in the bench matrix
06:55 - Lena: what benchmark metrics do you propose? p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (tokens/s), token efficiency (tokens per GPU-second), and cost per 1k tokens across variants
07:10 - Diego: exactly. also memory footprints, GPU utilization, and batch size sensitivity curves. we'll provide a spreadsheet with scenario sims (hit rates, batch sizes) and final per-token unit economics
07:25 - Maya: timeline: propose 4 weeks. week 0 (this week) collect traces and access, week1 baseline hosted runs, week2 dedicated runs + optimizations, week3 tuning and final report. customer ok?
07:42 - Samir: we need security review in parallel; we will need SOC2 docs and SSO/SAML details before any dedicated access
07:50 - Maya: yes we'll share SOC2 artifact link and a mini-security deck; Diego will follow up on network/VPC requirements
08:00 - Aisha: for success criteria let's capture these explicitly: 1) p95 < 2s for 400-token median workload; 2) cost per 1k tokens <= $0.03 with batching/caching applied (stretch goal); 3) quality delta < 2% on eval prompts vs current model
08:20 - Diego: good to have quantifiable pass/fail. we'll run A/B quality evals (automated scoring + small human review) and include regression alerts for the POC
08:35 - Tom: vendor comparisons — we're also running tests vs our on-prem cluster and a Bedrock run; curious to see relative unit economics
08:45 - Maya: noted, we'll include a competitor column (bedrock/self-host) in the spreadsheet.
08:55 - Aisha: are there specific instrumentation hooks we need to add to our app to capture traces?
09:05 - Diego: yes we'll ask you to export 7 days of request traces (timestamps, token counts, latency percentiles) or give read access to logs; we can also provide a small agent for synthetic load capture.
09:20 - Lena: for dedicated access what's the least-privilege network setup? we prefer VPC peering or private link rather than public endpoints
09:30 - Maya: we support VPC peering and private endpoints for Dedicated and Private deployments; we'll outline the exact ports and cert exchange in the next email
09:40 - Samir: ok what are the concrete next steps and owners?
09:45 - Maya: recap: (1) Zenith to send 7 days of traces and a list of representative prompts — owner Aisha — due EOD Thu; (2) Redwood to share cost-model spreadsheet and SOC2/security deck — owner Maya/Diego — due Mon; (3) Redwood to schedule hosted baseline benchmark and provide synthetic harness — owner Diego — target next Wed; (4) schedule 30m check-in after baseline to review numbers — owner Maya — proposed 2025-04-15
10:10 - Aisha: sounds good, will get traces to you.
10:15 - Diego: quick note on caching knobs: we'll test prefix caching, KV-cache for conversation, and response-level result caching for idempotent queries. each knob will be a toggle in our harness so we can measure incremental savings
10:30 - Tom: thanks, also please add an example run that shows savings with 30% cache hit rate for our template-heavy flows
10:38 - Maya: will do. any final questions?
10:45 - Samir: none here, thanks all
10:47 - Maya: thanks everyone, close out

Redwood to simulate trace-based cost model and return per-1k token estimates for hosted vs dedicated
